title: Thermal p99 dig + quick triage notes
content:
Context
- Observed recurring p99 latency spikes on cluster-7 (gpus: A100-80GB) between 09:30-10:15 local during high-concurrency runs. Spikes correlate with longer generation lengths (~800-1200 tokens) and periods of sustained high VRAM utilization.
- Initial hunch: thermal throttling causing kernel frequency step-down + CUDA scheduling jitter. Secondary: KV-cache eviction path causing large memcpy spikes when cache misses align with long seq lengths.

Quick reproduction notes (commands run today)
- k8s pod: redwood-runtime/serve-7 (node: g7-042)
- reproduce load: wrk-like harness: ./bench/loadgen -r 600 -c 40 -d 10m --seq-len 1000 --model rwd-7b-q8
- capture perf & nvml: sudo perf record -ag -o /tmp/pf.raw -- ./bench/loadgen ...
- nv-smi loop: while true; do nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,clocks.sm,clocks.mem --format=csv -l 1 >> /tmp/gpu-temp.csv; done &
- kernel trace: sudo bpftrace -e 'tracepoint:sys_enter_copy_to_user { @[comm] = count(); }' -o /tmp/bpf.trace (short run)

Raw observations from today's run
- Thermal ramp: node g7-042 GPU0 temp rose from 55C -> 84C over ~6 minutes, then clock rate dropped from 1530 MHz -> 1095 MHz; coincident with p99 jump from 230ms -> 890ms.
- VRAM: allocations peaked at 46GB (A100-80), fragmentation increased (many 64MB allocations seen in jemalloc logs).
- KV-cache: miss spikes aligned with p99: when miss rate > 18% for 3 consecutive seconds, memcpy ops (+copy_to_user) spiked.
- perf top (sampled) shows heavy time in aten::conv1d and our kernel_wrapper wrapper shims that do small copies per layer for quantized weights (hot path).

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Thermal throttling on sustained load causes GPU clock down and increases kernel execution time; combined w/ small-copy overheads yields tail amplification. (Primary)
2) KV-cache eviction & rehydration causes large synchronous memcpy to host -> device on misses, stalling other kernels. (Secondary)
3) Scheduler interference: long-running generation threads grabbing streams and not yielding while kernels block on memcopy, creating serialization at app layer. (Tertiary)

Immediate mitigation ideas (fast rollouts)
- Soft cap throughput per GPU: throttle concurrency for seq_len>600 to keep sustained power. Config: runtime heuristic: if seq_len_avg > 600 and avg_gpu_temp > 75C, cap inflight to 24. (short-term)
- Turn on asynchronous rehydration for KV-cache: background prefetch for top-k likely keys based on recent access. (short-medium)
- Increase mempool chunk size to reduce fragmentation (try 128MB chunks). (short)
- Kernel-level: reduce small memcpy calls by batching contiguous quant-weight copies in kernel_wrapper (needs PR). (medium)

Experiments to run (owner & metrics)
- EXP-therm-01: limit concurrency for long seqs on g7-042; measure p50/p95/p99, gpu_temp, throughput. Owner: @Daniel. Metric: p99 delta, tokens/sec, temp. (run 3x)
- EXP-kv-prefetch: enable async prefetch (prototype) in runtime branch daniel/async-prefetch; run against replay trace of today. Owner: @Samir. Metric: cache miss %, memcpy time, p99.
- EXP-mempool-128: adjust mempool chunk=128MB. Owner: @Maya. Metric: fragmentation (free list counts), alloc latency, p99.

Short-term TODO (today / next 2 days)
- [ ] Push config throttle patch to canary (runtime: routing/heuristics) - small rollback risk, testing in canary pool. (Daniel)
- [ ] Add nvml temp logging into per-request trace for canary (so we can correlate tail events to exact requests). (Samir)
- [ ] Prototype async prefetch skeleton and unit test KV metadata path. (Samir)
- [ ] Run mempool chunk experiment on two canary nodes (Maya)
- [ ] Draft incident blurb for #runtime-ops summarizing temp-throttle mitigation plan. (Daniel)
- [ ] Add ticket INF-4521 notes and link to PR once created. (All)

Longer-term follow-ups
- Investigate kernel_wrapper micro-optimizations: batch small copies; inline quant unpack; reduce kernel launches. (will require careful benching)
- Consider power/thermal-aware scheduling at cluster-level: assign long-seq workloads to cooler GPUs or nodes with better airflow; surface node thermal score in scheduler.
- Explore model-architecture tweaks: allow checkpointed generation state to reduce per-token memory churn for long sequences.

Quick debugging checklist for follow-up runs
- Ensure debug build (RT=debug) to get jemalloc and allocator traces.
- Start nvprof / Nsight to capture kernel timeline for a 60s window when spike starts.
- Run loadgen with replication of token length distribution (use yesterday's trace file: s3://bench/traces/2025-02-17-longseq.json)
- Collect /var/log/kern.log for OOM/driver warnings

Questions / unknowns to ask infra/ops
- Are there maintenance jobs (backup, snapshot) that coincide with 09:30 window on g7-042? (Ops)
- Is fan curve custom or default for that rack? Could we temporarily raise fan threshold? (Data center ops)

Notes to self / shorthand
- if thermal hypothesis false, next strongest is KV eviction. Watch memcpy time breakdown in perf.
- Check jemalloc stats in /proc for fragmentation; try purge_mode change test.
- Keep canary window narrow, have HP rollbacks ready.

Meeting notes (11:15 sync with Maya/Samir)
- Agreed to run mempool + throttle in parallel on different canaries.
- Samir to hand off async-prefetch PR by EOD tomorrow.
- Maya will produce quick dashboard with temp + p99 overlay for cluster-7.

References & commands pasted here for convenience
- Capture jemalloc stats: curl localhost:9090/debug/jemalloc | jq .
- Quick latency dump: curl localhost:8080/metrics?route=generate | grep p99
- Perf record & report: sudo perf record -F 99 -p $(pidof runtime) -g -- sleep 30; sudo perf script | c++filt | head -n 200

Next steps (tomorrow)
- Run EXP-therm-01 early (06:30) to avoid noisy co-tenants and iterate quickly.
- Re-evaluate after 3 successful runs; convene follow-up sync at 14:00.

End of scratchpad.
